title: Basel Framework — MAR (Minimum capital requirements for market risk)
sourceNote: Structured rendering of the BCBS consolidated Basel Framework, standard group MAR (market risk, incl. FRTB). Verbatim source: https://www.bis.org/basel_framework/standard/MAR.htm. Binds the bank via SARB Reg 38; FRTB-SA commencement per PA PC 18/2024.

sections.heading: Standardised approach to market risk
sections.text: The standardised approach computes market-risk capital as the sum of three components across the trading book.

subsections.text: Market-risk capital under the standardised approach is the simple sum of three components: the sensitivities-based method capital charge (delta, vega and curvature across risk classes), the default risk charge, and the residual risk add-on.

sections.heading: Internal models approach — expected shortfall
sections.text: A bank with supervisory approval may use an internal models approach for market-risk capital based on expected shortfall.

subsections.text: The internal models approach measures risk using an expected shortfall (ES) model calibrated to a 97.5% one-tailed confidence level, capturing the tail risk of the trading portfolio over a liquidity-horizon-adjusted holding period.

sections.heading: Transitional and legacy market-risk treatment
sections.text: Pending full FRTB adoption, the legacy (Basel 2.5) internal-models market-risk treatment may continue to apply.

subsections.text: Legacy internal-models market-risk capital is based on value-at-risk (VaR) computed at a 99% one-tailed confidence level over a minimum one-year (approximately 250 business day) historical observation window, supplemented by a stressed VaR over a period of significant financial stress.
